name: P1-practo
prompt: Below are 6 numbered screenshots of the Practo mobile app (Android) captured by the owner as a DESIGN REFERENCE (call them P1..P6 in the order provided). For EACH screenshot: (1) identify the screen (home, search, doctor listing, doctor profile, clinic/hospital page, booking flow, filters, orders, chat, health hub, account, etc.), (2) describe its visual design in depth: layout structure, list/card design, PHOTO usage (are doctor/clinic photos shown? circular avatars? sizes?), typography hierarchy (sizes/weights), the color system (what reads as primary vs secondary/accent color; approximate hex), components (chips, badges, pills, tabs, bottom nav, ratings, buttons, banners), spacing/density feel, (3) name the ONE design element that most makes this screen feel premium/desirable. This informs a redesign of another Indian healthcare booking app, so extract transferable patterns. Be concrete and honest.
verdict:
# Practo Reference Screens — Detailed Breakdown

## P1 — Onboarding / Login (Slide 1: Video Consult)

**Screen type:** Onboarding carousel + phone-number login (single persistent screen; only the illustration/hero changes per slide).

**Layout:** Vertical split. Top ~70% is a deep indigo-blue brand field (`#3A3F9E`–`#3B44AC` range) containing logo, illustration, headline, carousel dots. Bottom ~30% is a white sheet with the login form. The hard color break between blue field and white sheet is the whole composition.

**Visual details:**
- Logo: white "practo" wordmark flanked by two cyan dots (`#12CDC4` / `#4AC9F0`-ish) — instantly recognizable.
- Illustration: flat vector art, doctor emerging from a phone with stethoscope — friendly, human, on-message. Muted orange/teal accents against the blue.
- Headline: white, bold, ~22–24sp, two lines, sentence case ("Video consult top doctors from the comfort of your home") — benefit-led, not feature-led.
- Carousel: back chevron + 3 dots (active dot white/larger, inactive faint).
- Form: label "Let's get started! Enter your mobile number" in near-black semibold (~18sp); input row = "+91 ▾ | Mobile number" in a large rounded-rectangle bordered field (~8–10dp radius, 1dp grey border, ~56–64dp tall) with a thin vertical divider between country code and number.
- "Trouble signing in?" — underlined dark text link, bottom-left. Notably there's **no visible CTA button** (OTP fires on valid entry) — friction-reduction choice.

**Typography hierarchy:** Logo > headline (bold, white) > form label (dark, semibold) > placeholder (grey). Clean 3-level hierarchy, generous line-height on the headline.

**Colors:** Primary = indigo brand blue (~`#3B44AC`); accent = cyan dots/teal; neutral grey borders; white sheet. No gradients — flat, confident.

**Density/spacing:** Very airy. One input on the whole screen. Whitespace is the design.

**Premium element:** The **flat custom illustration set on the saturated brand-blue field** — it signals "real brand with real designers" and turns a utilitarian OTP gate into a marketing moment.

**Transferable:** Keep login visual weight low; one field; the onboarding carousel lives *above* the form permanently, never blocking it.

---

## P2 — Onboarding (Slide 2: Patient Stories)

Same screen template as P1; only hero content changes.

- Illustration: hand holding a phone showing review cards with tiny doctor avatars + 4–5 gold stars — a literal mini-preview of the product's review-card pattern inside the artwork. Smart: the illustration teaches the UI.
- Headline: "Read patients' stories and book doctor appointments" — same white bold treatment.
- Second dot active (white), first/third faint.
- Form identical to P1 — zero layout shift between slides, so swiping feels stable and calm.

**Premium element:** The illustration doubling as a **product preview with star ratings** — social proof embedded in the artwork itself.

**Transferable:** Carousel slides should each carry one concrete promise (consult / reviews / scale) and never disturb the form below.

---

## P3 — Onboarding (Slide 3: Trust/Scale Claim)

Same template, third slide.

- Illustration: doctor with crossed arms and stethoscope in front of a crowd of muted-people silhouettes arranged in a heart/V shape — reads as "trusted by the many."
- Headline: "**1 Crore Indians** connect with doctor every year on Practo" — a scale/trust number, localized units (crore). Numbers in headlines are the strongest trust device here.
- Third dot active. Form unchanged.

**Premium element:** The **quantified social-proof headline** (1 Crore) — specific scale numbers outperform generic "trusted by millions."

**Transferable:** End onboarding on a big localized trust stat. Keep the three-slide arc: value → proof → scale.

---

## P4 — Home Screen with Location-Permission Dialog

**Screen type:** Home (post-login) with a modal "Search your location" dialog overlaid; scrim over content.

**Layout:** Modal card (white, ~16dp radius) floats near the top over a dimmed home screen. Behind the scrim you can see the home skeleton: location header, promo banner ("See your savings →"), two large consultation tiles, a 4-up icon action row, a Diwali promo banner, and the bottom nav.

**Dialog details:**
- Left: outlined location-pin illustration with a cyan check badge; right: title "Search your location" (black, bold, ~20sp) + grey subtitle two-liner. X close at top-right.
- Two full-width stacked buttons: **filled cyan "Enable Location"** (white text, ~12dp radius, primary) above **outlined "Search Locality"** (cyan text, cyan 1dp border). Clear primary/secondary pairing, same height, 12dp gap.
- Action hierarchy is textbook: explain benefit → offer easy primary → manual fallback → escape hatch.

**Home content glimpsed (dimmed):**
- Two large tiles "In-Person Consultation" / "Video Consultation" with **real human photos** (female doctor with stethoscope; male doctor waving on a phone screen) — photos bleed to tile edges.
- 4 white icon cards: Book Lab Tests, Plan Surgeries, Order Medicines, Get Practo Shield — last one is dark navy with gold shield + mint-green "Save ₹20,000" pill.
- Bottom nav: floating white pill container (fully rounded, shadow) with 4 items; **Home tab is a solid indigo filled circle with white icon** — a strong active-state treatment. Labels beneath icons.

**Colors:** Cyan/blue as action color (`#29A9EA`-ish), indigo as brand/active-nav, gold as monetization accent, green as savings badge.

**Premium element:** The **floating pill bottom-nav with a filled-circle active tab** — it floats above content, feels modern/iOS-native, and elevates the whole app shell.

**Transferable:** Location onboarding as a benefit-stated modal with dual CTA; permission dialogs should look like product UI, not OS dialogs.

---

## P5 — Home Screen (Full)

**Screen type:** Home.

**Layout (top→bottom):**
1. Location header: pin icon + "Bangalore" bold white ~26sp + chevron — location as a primary, tappable control.
2. Search: large white pill (~64dp tall, full radius) "Search for" with magnifier icon, occupying ~70% width; beside it an **"Ask Care AI"** chip — white pill with cyan sparkle/gradient border. AI feature surfaced as a peer of search, not buried.
3. **Practo SHIELD hero:** full-bleed dark-navy panel with a glowing gold shield graphic. Golden metallic pill "•practo• SHIELD @₹1,999/year", gold subhead "Your family's health plan", white body "11 Free Hospital Visits & Unlimited GP Video Consultations*", ghost-outline pill CTA "See your savings →". This is a premium membership upsell given luxury treatment (gold-on-navy, glows, curved planet-horizon line at the panel bottom).
4. White rounded sheet: two large photo tiles (In-Person / Video Consultation) — light-blue gradient backgrounds with real doctor photos anchored right, labels top-left in dark semibold.
5. 4-up action cards: three white cards with **black outlined icons with a single blue accent detail** (test tube, hand+cross, pills), plus the dark-navy Shield card with gold shield + mint "Save ₹20,000" badge.
6. Horizontal promo carousel ("Affordable Procedures by Expert Doctors…" blue banner) peeking.

**Photos:** Real photography (not illustration) for consultations — light, clinical, friendly Indian-doctor imagery. Photos appear inside tiles, not circular avatars.

**Typography:** Location and tile titles ~18–22sp semibold; body 14–16sp; weight contrast (semibold dark headers vs regular grey) carries hierarchy without size jumps.

**Colors:** Deep navy base up top, white sheet below, cyan/blue utility accents, **gold strictly reserved for the paid product**, mint green for savings. That restraint is the sophistication.

**Premium element:** The **gold-on-navy SHIELD hero panel** — a membership product rendered like a credit-card/gold-tier visual. It monetizes while making the app feel premium.

**Transferable:** (a) Floating pill nav; (b) search bar + AI chip as one row; (c) two big consultation tiles as the core actions; (d) icon cards where one accent color keeps outlined icons lively; (e) reserve a "luxury color" (gold) exclusively for the paid tier.

---

## P6 — Home / Speciality Browse + Q&A Feed

**Screen type:** Home continuation — speciality discovery grid + community Q&A feed (scroll state below P5).

**Layout:**
1. Sticky-ish top bar: light-grey pill search "Search for Special…" + "Ask Care AI" chip (gradient border) — search persists on scroll.
2. Section header "Find doctors by speciality" — black bold ~22sp.
3. White card containing a **segmented control**: "General Care" (active = white pill with shadow inside a grey track) vs "Advanced Care" (grey text) — soft iOS-style segmented tabs.
4. **2-row horizontal-scroll grid of speciality tiles**: rounded photo cards (~150×170dp) with real photography — General Physician (male doctor, white coat, stethoscope), Women's Health, Skin Specialist, Dentist, Eye Specialist, ENT (with blue glow highlighting the affected body part!). Photos fade to white at the bottom; label in dark semibold centered at bottom. 4th column peeks, signaling scrollability.
5. Section "Free Expert Q&A" + cyan "Explore all ›" link (right-aligned, standard list-header pattern).
6. **Q&A cards**: white cards with a small circular blue icon (people), "Community Question" semibold + grey "16h ago" timestamp, and a **mint-green "Answered" pill badge** right-aligned. Below, a nested white rounded text box with the question preview (2–3 lines, ellipsized) and a doctor-avatars row beneath (answerer preview).
7. Floating pill bottom nav over content.

**Photos:** Heavy real-photo usage — specialities are communicated photographically (procedures, body areas), which is far clearer than icons. Circular avatars only appear small, in Q&A meta rows.

**Typography:** Section headers bold dark ~22sp; tile labels ~16sp semibold; metadata 13–14sp grey. Hierarchy via weight + color, not many sizes.

**Colors:** Now mostly white/light-grey cards on a pale background; cyan links; green status badge; blue icon accents. Calmer than the navy top of P5 — the home has a dark "brand zone" and a light "utility zone."

**Density:** Comfortable-medium; cards ~12–16dp gutters, 16dp radius, subtle or no shadows (elevation via card-on-grey contrast).

**Premium element:** The **photographic speciality grid** — real, well-shot, body-area-highlighted imagery (ENT with blue glow) makes the catalog feel clinically credible and visually rich, unlike generic icon grids.

**Transferable:** (a) Segmented "General/Advanced Care" filter over a photo grid; (b) horizontally peeking 2-row card grid; (c) Q&A cards with status pill + timestamp + nested question bubble — a great trust-content pattern for a home feed.

---

## Cross-Screen Transferable System Summary

1. **Two-zone color architecture:** dark navy brand zone (header/hero/upsell) → white sheet (utility content). Gives identity *and* readability.
2. **Color discipline:** cyan/blue = actions & links; **gold = paid tier only**; mint green = savings/status. Never mixed.
3. **Photography strategy:** illustrations only in onboarding; real photos everywhere in product (tiles, specialities). Photos do the explaining; text stays short.
4. **Floating pill bottom nav with filled-circle active tab** — the single most distinctive shell component.
5. **Persistent onboarding-form pattern:** carousel above, form below, zero reflow.
6. **Search + AI as peers in one row; location as a big header control.**
7. **Everything rounded:** pills, cards, buttons at 12–16dp+ radius; minimal shadows, elevation via background contrast.
8. **Benefit-stated permission dialogs** with filled-primary + outlined-secondary CTAs.
9. **Specificity in copy:** "1 Crore Indians", "₹1,999/year", "Save ₹20,000", "11 Free Visits" — concrete numbers everywhere instead of vague claims.
